items.title: We are {{accent}}.
items.label: 0ff The Print · vol. 1
items.photo_alt: Editorial still life: chrome italic 0 sculpture wrapped in pink leopard print ribbon with electric blue dye drip on glossy black surface
items.body:
Every city has an underground. Most of them wait for a camera to find it. Ours doesn't wait. We *are* the camera, the chair, the bench, the board. The set that ended before the algorithm woke up, the ink going in on a Friday afternoon, the master printing at 4AM. That current runs through this desk.

Fridays at Zenhouse. The Mix on the Strip. Rah Rah Room. Paper Tiger. The rooms know us by name now, and the names on our roster aren't archetypes anymore.

We're not covering the scene. We're the reason it has a pulse you can find. San Antonio first. Then Texas: Austin, Houston, Dallas. The state hears it from us or it doesn't hear it.

You find us through the work. That's still the deal.

items.title: The cards were {{accent}}.
items.label: Media house now
items.photo_alt: Night portrait in a diner booth by the window, teal light, from the August 17 night set
items.body:
When this started there was no content. That's the truth of it. The roster got drawn as archetypes and the cards stood in for people, because cards were what we had.

Three weeks of nights changed that. Zenhouse, the Mix, the raves, the arcade, a night set walking the Strip. The folders are full now. Real frames, our rooms, no stock. Scroll up, that grid is all ours.

So 0FF THE PRINT runs as what it already became: a media house inside the underground. The cards stay, they're the roster's ID system now. But the work leads.

items.title: The roster stopped being {{accent}}.
items.label: Seats are filling
items.photo_alt: Concept art: giant pink neon heartbeat waveform forming a heart over a black and electric blue city grid at night
items.body:
The roster started as archetypes, the seats a scene needs filled before it can call itself one. Two of them just got names.

THE VOICE: KAV-MAN. San Antonio rapper. What he's loading stays off the page until it drops. When it drops, it drops with our frames on it.

THE ENGINEER: VIRGOSGATEWAY. Producer, engineer, credits already sitting in your library without his name on your lips. Sessions closed. File pending.

Not subjects. Members. The takeover has a soundtrack now. Pull the cards below.

items.title: The format moves to {{accent}}.
items.label: The Ink
items.photo_alt: Back-of-head editorial portrait of long pastel-pink dyed hair with chrome scissors in frame, pink leopard belt accent
items.body:
The rule since 001: the subject does their work on camera while they talk. Never a sit-down against a wall. The chair set it, color happening mid-conversation, gothic essay energy with foils in.

002 takes the same rule to a tattoo bench. Black and grey by appointment, oil on canvas after hours. Two cameras, four to six minutes, room light stays the room light. No grade fighting the subject's own work.

The subject sees the cut before anyone else does. That's the house rule, and it's in writing.

items.title: Why {{accent}}.
items.label: Off the record · stays off the record
items.photo_alt: Editorial still life: vintage chrome microphone on glossy black with torn pink leopard fabric strip, closed pink notebook with chrome lock, single blue dye drop
items.body: Because we said so. This isn't a place for people to fight. It's a place for the work. If you want to talk to the desk, DM *@vamppsych*. Off the record stays off the record.
